units.rightText: And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.

units.leftText: I, Daniel, was grieved in my spirit, and the visions in my mind alarmed me.
units.rightText: As for me, Daniel, my spirit was grieved in the midst of my body, and the visions of my head troubled me.

units.leftText: I approached one of those who were standing there, and I asked him the true meaning of all this.
units.rightText: I came near unto one of them that stood by, and asked him the truth concerning all this. So he told me, and made me know the interpretation of the things.

units.leftText: ‘These four great beasts are four kings who will arise from the earth.
units.rightText: These great beasts, which are four, are four kings, that shall arise out of the earth.

units.leftText: But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever — yes, forever and ever.’
units.rightText: But the saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever.

units.leftText: Then I wanted to know the true meaning of the fourth beast, which was different from all the others — extremely terrifying — devouring and crushing with iron teeth and bronze claws, then trampling underfoot whatever was left.
units.rightText: Then I desired to know the truth concerning the fourth beast, which was diverse from all of them, exceeding terrible, whose teeth were of iron, and its nails of brass; which devoured, brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet;

units.leftText: I also wanted to know about the ten horns on its head and the other horn that came up, before which three of them fell— the horn whose appearance was more imposing than the others, with eyes and with a mouth that spoke words of arrogance.
units.rightText: and concerning the ten horns that were on its head, and the other horn which came up, and before which three fell, even that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spake great things, whose look was more stout than its fellows.

units.leftText: As I watched, this horn was waging war against the saints and prevailing against them,
units.rightText: I beheld, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against them;

units.leftText: until the Ancient of Days arrived and pronounced judgment in favor of the saints of the Most High, and the time came for them to possess the kingdom.
units.rightText: until the ancient of days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the Most High, and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom.

units.leftText: This is what he said: ‘The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will appear on the earth, different from all the other kingdoms, and it will devour the whole earth, trample it down, and crush it.
units.rightText: Thus he said, The fourth beast shall be a fourth kingdom upon earth, which shall be diverse from all the kingdoms, and shall devour the whole earth, and shall tread it down, and break it in pieces.

units.leftText: And the ten horns are ten kings who will rise from this kingdom. After them another king, different from the earlier ones, will rise and subdue three kings.
units.rightText: And as for the ten horns, out of this kingdom shall ten kings arise: and another shall arise after them; and he shall be diverse from the former, and he shall put down three kings.

units.leftText: He will speak out against the Most High and oppress the saints of the Most High, intending to change the appointed times and laws; and the saints will be given into his hand for a time, and times, and half a time.
units.rightText: And he shall speak words against the Most High, and shall wear out the saints of the Most High; and he shall think to change the times and the law; and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and half a time.

units.leftText: But the court will convene, and his dominion will be taken away and completely destroyed forever.
units.rightText: But the judgment shall be set, and they shall take away his dominion, to consume and to destroy it unto the end.

units.leftText: Then the sovereignty, dominion, and greatness of the kingdoms under all of heaven will be given to the people, the saints of the Most High. His kingdom will be an everlasting kingdom, and all rulers will serve and obey Him.’
units.rightText: And the kingdom and the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High: his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.

units.leftText: Thus ends the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts troubled me greatly, and my face turned pale. But I kept the matter to myself.”
units.rightText: Here is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts much troubled me, and my countenance was changed in me: but I kept the matter in my heart.

units.leftText: In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, subsequent to the one that had appeared to me earlier.
units.rightText: In the third year of the reign of king Belshazzar a vision appeared unto me, even unto me, Daniel, after that which appeared unto me at the first.

units.leftText: And in the vision I saw myself in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam. I saw in the vision that I was beside the Ulai Canal.
units.rightText: And I saw in the vision; now it was so, that when I saw, I was in Shushan the palace, which is in the province of Elam; and I saw in the vision, and I was by the river Ulai.

units.leftText: Then I lifted up my eyes and saw a ram with two horns standing beside the canal. The horns were long, but one was longer than the other, and the longer one grew up later.
units.rightText: Then I lifted up mine eyes, and saw, and, behold, there stood before the river a ram which had two horns: and the two horns were high; but one was higher than the other, and the higher came up last.

units.leftText: I saw the ram charging toward the west and the north and the south. No animal could stand against him, and there was no deliverance from his power. He did as he pleased and became great.
units.rightText: I saw the ram pushing westward, and northward, and southward; and no beasts could stand before him, neither was there any that could deliver out of his hand; but he did according to his will, and magnified himself.

units.leftText: As I was contemplating all this, suddenly a goat with a prominent horn between his eyes came out of the west, crossing the surface of the entire earth without touching the ground.
units.rightText: And as I was considering, behold, a he-goat came from the west over the face of the whole earth, and touched not the ground: and the goat had a notable horn between his eyes.

units.leftText: He came toward the two-horned ram I had seen standing beside the canal and rushed at him with furious power.
units.rightText: And he came to the ram that had the two horns, which I saw standing before the river, and ran upon him in the fury of his power.

units.leftText: I saw him approach the ram in a rage against him, and he struck the ram and shattered his two horns. The ram was powerless to stand against him, and the goat threw him to the ground and trampled him, and no one could deliver the ram from his power.
units.rightText: And I saw him come close unto the ram, and he was moved with anger against him, and smote the ram, and brake his two horns; and there was no power in the ram to stand before him; but he cast him down to the ground, and trampled upon him; and there was none that could deliver the ram out of his hand.

units.leftText: Thus the goat became very great, but at the height of his power, his large horn was broken off, and four prominent horns came up in its place, pointing toward the four winds of heaven.
units.rightText: And the he-goat magnified himself exceedingly: and when he was strong, the great horn was broken; and instead of it there came up four notable horns toward the four winds of heaven.

units.leftText: From one of these horns a little horn emerged and grew extensively toward the south and the east and toward the Beautiful Land.
units.rightText: And out of one of them came forth a little horn, which waxed exceeding great, toward the south, and toward the east, and toward the glorious land.

units.leftText: It grew as high as the host of heaven, and it cast down some of the host and some of the stars to the earth and trampled them.
units.rightText: And it waxed great, even to the host of heaven; and some of the host and of the stars it cast down to the ground, and trampled upon them.

units.leftText: It magnified itself, even to the Prince of the host; it removed His daily sacrifice and overthrew the place of His sanctuary.
units.rightText: Yea, it magnified itself, even to the prince of the host; and it took away from him the continual burnt-offering, and the place of his sanctuary was cast down.

units.leftText: And in the rebellion, the host and the daily sacrifice were given over to the horn, and it flung truth to the ground and prospered in whatever it did.
units.rightText: And the host was given over to it together with the continual burnt-offering through transgression; and it cast down truth to the ground, and it did its pleasure and prospered.
leftNotes: 8:12 Or on account of transgression

units.leftText: Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to him, “How long until the fulfillment of the vision of the daily sacrifice, the rebellion that causes desolation, and the surrender of the sanctuary and of the host to be trampled?”
units.rightText: Then I heard a holy one speaking; and another holy one said unto that certain one who spake, How long shall be the vision concerning the continual burnt-offering, and the transgression that maketh desolate, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot?

units.leftText: He said to me, “It will take 2,300 evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be properly restored.” Gabriel Interprets Daniel’s Vision
units.rightText: And he said unto me, Unto two thousand and three hundred evenings and mornings; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed.

units.leftText: While I, Daniel, was watching the vision and trying to understand it, there stood before me one having the appearance of a man.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when I, even I Daniel, had seen the vision, that I sought to understand it; and, behold, there stood before me as the appearance of a man.

units.leftText: And I heard the voice of a man calling from between the banks of the Ulai: “Gabriel, explain the vision to this man.”
units.rightText: And I heard a man’s voice between the banks of the Ulai, which called, and said, Gabriel, make this man to understand the vision.

units.leftText: As he came near to where I stood, I was terrified and fell facedown. “Son of man,” he said to me, “understand that the vision concerns the time of the end.”
units.rightText: So he came near where I stood; and when he came, I was affrighted, and fell upon my face: but he said unto me, Understand, O son of man; for the vision belongeth to the time of the end.

units.leftText: While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground.
units.rightText: Now as he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face toward the ground; but he touched me, and set me upright.

units.leftText: and said, “Behold, I will make known to you what will happen in the latter time of wrath, because it concerns the appointed time of the end.
units.rightText: And he said, Behold, I will make thee know what shall be in the latter time of the indignation; for it belongeth to the appointed time of the end.

units.leftText: The two-horned ram that you saw represents the kings of Media and Persia.
units.rightText: The ram which thou sawest, that had the two horns, they are the kings of Media and Persia.

units.leftText: The shaggy goat represents the king of Greece, and the large horn between his eyes is the first king.
units.rightText: And the rough he-goat is the king of Greece: and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king.
leftNotes: 8:21 Hebrew of Javan

units.leftText: The four horns that replaced the broken one represent four kingdoms that will rise from that nation but will not have the same power.
units.rightText: And as for that which was broken, in the place whereof four stood up, four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not with his power.

units.leftText: In the latter part of their reign, when the rebellion has reached its full measure, an insolent king, skilled in intrigue, will come to the throne.
units.rightText: And in the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors are come to the full, a king of fierce countenance, and understanding dark sentences, shall stand up.

units.leftText: His power will be great, but it will not be his own. He will cause terrible destruction and succeed in whatever he does. He will destroy the mighty men along with the holy people.
units.rightText: And his power shall be mighty, but not by his own power; and he shall destroy wonderfully, and shall prosper and do his pleasure; and he shall destroy the mighty ones and the holy people.

units.leftText: Through his craft and by his hand, he will cause deceit to prosper, and in his own mind he will make himself great. In a time of peace he will destroy many, and he will even stand against the Prince of princes. Yet he will be broken off, but not by human hands.
units.rightText: And through his policy he shall cause craft to prosper in his hand; and he shall magnify himself in his heart, and in their security shall he destroy many: he shall also stand up against the prince of princes; but he shall be broken without hand.

units.leftText: The vision of the evenings and the mornings that has been spoken is true. Now you must seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future.”
units.rightText: And the vision of the evenings and mornings which hath been told is true: but shut thou up the vision; for it belongeth to many days to come.

units.leftText: I, Daniel, was exhausted and lay ill for days. Then I got up and went about the king’s business. I was confounded by the vision; it was beyond understanding.
units.rightText: And I, Daniel, fainted, and was sick certain days; then I rose up, and did the king’s business: and I wondered at the vision, but none understood it.

units.leftText: In the first year of Darius son of Xerxes, a Mede by descent, who was made ruler over the kingdom of the Chaldeans —
units.rightText: In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, who was made king over the realm of the Chaldeans,
leftNotes: 9:1 Hebrew Ahasuerus
9:1 That is, the Babylonians

units.leftText: in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the sacred books, according to the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet, that the desolation of Jerusalem would last seventy years.
units.rightText: in the first year of his reign I, Daniel, understood by the books the number of the years whereof the word of Jehovah came to Jeremiah the prophet, for the accomplishing of the desolations of Jerusalem, even seventy years.
leftNotes: 9:2 See Jeremiah 25:11–12|JER 25:11-12* and Jeremiah 29:10.

units.leftText: So I turned my attention to the Lord God to seek Him by prayer and petition, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
units.rightText: And I set my face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.

units.leftText: And I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed, “O, Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps His covenant of loving devotion to those who love Him and keep His commandments,
units.rightText: And I prayed unto Jehovah my God, and made confession, and said, Oh, Lord, the great and dreadful God, who keepeth covenant and lovingkindness with them that love him and keep his commandments,
leftNotes: 9:4 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: we have sinned and done wrong. We have acted wickedly and rebelled. We have turned away from Your commandments and ordinances.
units.rightText: we have sinned, and have dealt perversely, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even turning aside from thy precepts and from thine ordinances;

units.leftText: We have not listened to Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, leaders, fathers, and all the people of the land.
units.rightText: neither have we hearkened unto thy servants the prophets, that spake in thy name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.

units.leftText: To You, O Lord, belongs righteousness, but this day we are covered with shame— the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, and all Israel near and far, in all the countries to which You have driven us because of our unfaithfulness to You.
units.rightText: O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of face, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee.

units.leftText: O LORD, we are covered with shame — our kings, our leaders, and our fathers — because we have sinned against You.
units.rightText: O Lord, to us belongeth confusion of face, to our kings, to our princes, and to our fathers, because we have sinned against thee.

units.leftText: To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, even though we have rebelled against Him
units.rightText: To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgiveness; for we have rebelled against him;

units.leftText: and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God to walk in His laws, which He set before us through His servants the prophets.
units.rightText: neither have we obeyed the voice of Jehovah our God, to walk in his laws, which he set before us by his servants the prophets.

units.leftText: All Israel has transgressed Your law and turned away, refusing to obey Your voice; so the oath and the curse written in the Law of Moses the servant of God has been poured out on us, because we have sinned against You.
units.rightText: Yea, all Israel have transgressed thy law, even turning aside, that they should not obey thy voice: therefore hath the curse been poured out upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of God; for we have sinned against him.

units.leftText: You have carried out the words spoken against us and against our rulers by bringing upon us a great disaster. For under all of heaven, nothing has ever been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And he hath confirmed his words, which he spake against us, and against our judges that judged us, by bringing upon us a great evil; for under the whole heaven hath not been done as hath been done upon Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Just as it is written in the Law of Moses, all this disaster has come upon us, yet we have not sought the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our iniquities and giving attention to Your truth.
units.rightText: As it is written in the law of Moses, all this evil is come upon us: yet have we not entreated the favor of Jehovah our God, that we should turn from our iniquities, and have discernment in thy truth.

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD has kept the calamity in store and brought it upon us. For the LORD our God is righteous in all He does; yet we have not obeyed His voice.
units.rightText: Therefore hath Jehovah watched over the evil, and brought it upon us; for Jehovah our God is righteous in all his works which he doeth, and we have not obeyed his voice.

units.leftText: Now, O Lord our God, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and who made for Yourself a name renowned to this day, we have sinned; we have acted wickedly.
units.rightText: And now, O Lord our God, that hast brought thy people forth out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and hast gotten thee renown, as at this day; we have sinned, we have done wickedly.

units.leftText: O Lord, in keeping with all Your righteous acts, I pray that Your anger and wrath may turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain; for because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people are a reproach to all around us.
units.rightText: O Lord, according to all thy righteousness, let thine anger and thy wrath, I pray thee, be turned away from thy city Jerusalem, thy holy mountain; because for our sins, and for the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and thy people are become a reproach to all that are round about us.

units.leftText: So now, our God, hear the prayers and petitions of Your servant. For Your sake, O Lord, cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary.
units.rightText: Now therefore, O our God, hearken unto the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplications, and cause thy face to shine upon thy sanctuary that is desolate, for the Lord’s sake.

units.leftText: Incline Your ear, O my God, and hear; open Your eyes and see the desolation of the city that bears Your name. For we are not presenting our petitions before You because of our righteous acts, but because of Your great compassion.
units.rightText: O my God, incline thine ear, and hear; open thine eyes, and behold our desolations, and the city which is called by thy name: for we do not present our supplications before thee for our righteousnesses, but for thy great mercies’ sake.

units.leftText: O Lord, listen! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, hear and act! For Your sake, O my God, do not delay, because Your city and Your people bear Your name.” Gabriel’s Prophecy of the Seventy Weeks
units.rightText: O Lord, hear; O Lord, forgive; O Lord, hearken and do; defer not, for thine own sake, O my God, because thy city and thy people are called by thy name.

units.leftText: While I was speaking, praying, confessing my sin and that of my people Israel, and presenting my petition before the LORD my God concerning His holy mountain—
units.rightText: And while I was speaking, and praying, and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before Jehovah my God for the holy mountain of my God;

units.leftText: while I was still praying, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening sacrifice.
units.rightText: yea, while I was speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening oblation.

units.leftText: He instructed me and spoke with me, saying: “O Daniel, I have come now to give you insight and understanding.
units.rightText: And he instructed me, and talked with me, and said, O Daniel, I am now come forth to give thee wisdom and understanding.

units.leftText: At the beginning of your petitions, an answer went out, and I have come to tell you, for you are highly precious. So consider the message and understand the vision:
units.rightText: At the beginning of thy supplications the commandment went forth, and I am come to tell thee; for thou art greatly beloved: therefore consider the matter, and understand the vision.

units.leftText: Seventy weeks are decreed for your people and your holy city to stop their transgression, to put an end to sin, to make atonement for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Most Holy Place.
units.rightText: Seventy weeks are decreed upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most holy.
leftNotes: 9:24 Or Seventy sevens; also twice in verse 25 and once in verse 26
9:24 Or the Holy of Holies or the Most Holy One; literally the Most Holy

units.leftText: Know and understand this: From the issuance of the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Messiah, the Prince, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It will be rebuilt with streets and a trench, but in times of distress.
units.rightText: Know therefore and discern, that from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem unto the anointed one, the prince, shall be seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks: it shall be built again, with street and moat, even in troublous times.
leftNotes: 9:25 Or the Anointed One; also in verse 26

units.leftText: Then after the sixty-two weeks the Messiah will be cut off and will have nothing.
units.rightText: And after the threescore and two weeks shall the anointed one be cut off, and shall have nothing: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and even unto the end shall be war; desolations are determined.
leftNotes: 9:26 Hebrew Then after sixty-two sevens

units.leftText: And he will confirm a covenant with many for one week, but in the middle of the week he will put an end to sacrifice and offering. And on the wing of the temple will come the abomination that causes desolation, until the decreed destruction is poured out upon him. ”
units.rightText: And he shall make a firm covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease; and upon the wing of abominations shall come one that maketh desolate; and even unto the full end, and that determined, shall wrath be poured out upon the desolate.
leftNotes: 9:27 Or for one seven; similarly again in this verse
9:27 Literally And on the wing (will come) the abomination that causes desolation, or And on the wing of abominations (will come) one who causes desolation,
9:27 Literally until the decreed consummation is poured out upon (him who) is desolate.

units.leftText: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a message was revealed to Daniel, who was called Belteshazzar. The message was true, and it concerned a great conflict. And the understanding of the message was given to him in a vision.
units.rightText: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a thing was revealed unto Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the thing was true, even a great warfare: and he understood the thing, and had understanding of the vision.
leftNotes: 10:1 Or true and greatly burdensome

units.leftText: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three full weeks.
units.rightText: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning three whole weeks.

units.leftText: I ate no rich food, no meat or wine entered my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with oil until the three weeks were completed.
units.rightText: I ate no pleasant bread, neither came flesh nor wine into my mouth, neither did I anoint myself at all, till three whole weeks were fulfilled.

units.leftText: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, as I was standing on the bank of the great river, the Tigris,
units.rightText: And in the four and twentieth day of the first month, as I was by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel,

units.leftText: I lifted up my eyes, and behold, there was a certain man dressed in linen, with a belt of fine gold from Uphaz around his waist.
units.rightText: I lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and, behold, a man clothed in linen, whose loins were girded with pure gold of Uphaz:

units.leftText: His body was like beryl, his face like the brilliance of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of polished bronze, and his voice like the sound of a multitude.
units.rightText: his body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as flaming torches, and his arms and his feet like unto burnished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.

units.leftText: Only I, Daniel, saw the vision; the men with me did not see it, but a great terror fell upon them, and they ran and hid themselves.
units.rightText: And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision; for the men that were with me saw not the vision; but a great quaking fell upon them, and they fled to hide themselves.

units.leftText: So I was left alone, gazing at this great vision. No strength remained in me; my face grew deathly pale, and I was powerless.
units.rightText: So I was left alone, and saw this great vision, and there remained no strength in me; for my comeliness was turned in me into corruption, and I retained no strength.

units.leftText: I heard the sound of his words, and as I listened, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground.
units.rightText: Yet heard I the voice of his words; and when I heard the voice of his words, then was I fallen into a deep sleep on my face, with my face toward the ground.

units.leftText: Suddenly, a hand touched me and set me trembling on my hands and knees.
units.rightText: And, behold, a hand touched me, which set me upon my knees and upon the palms of my hands.

units.leftText: He said to me, “Daniel, you are a man who is highly precious. Consider carefully the words that I am about to say to you. Stand up, for I have now been sent to you.” And when he had said this to me, I stood up trembling.
units.rightText: And he said unto me, O Daniel, thou man greatly beloved, understand the words that I speak unto thee, and stand upright; for unto thee am I now sent. And when he had spoken this word unto me, I stood trembling.

units.leftText: “Do not be afraid, Daniel,” he said, “for from the first day that you purposed to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come in response to them.
units.rightText: Then said he unto me, Fear not, Daniel; for from the first day that thou didst set thy heart to understand, and to humble thyself before thy God, thy words were heard: and I am come for thy words’ sake.

units.leftText: However, the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, for I had been left there with the kings of Persia.
units.rightText: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me one and twenty days; but, lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me: and I remained there with the kings of Persia.

units.leftText: Now I have come to explain to you what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision concerns those days.”
units.rightText: Now I am come to make thee understand what shall befall thy people in the latter days; for the vision is yet for many days.

units.leftText: While he was speaking these words to me, I set my face toward the ground and became speechless.
units.rightText: And when he had spoken unto me according to these words, I set my face toward the ground, and was dumb.

units.leftText: And suddenly one with the likeness of a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and said to the one standing before me, “My lord, because of the vision, I am overcome with anguish, and I have no strength.
units.rightText: And, behold, one in the likeness of the sons of men touched my lips: then I opened my mouth, and spake and said unto him that stood before me, O my lord, by reason of the vision my sorrows are turned upon me, and I retain no strength.
leftNotes: 10:16 Most MT manuscripts; literally with the likeness of sons of man; DSS, LXX, and one MT manuscript with the likeness of the hand of a man

units.leftText: How can I, your servant, speak with you, my lord? Now I have no strength, nor is any breath left in me.”
units.rightText: For how can the servant of this my lord talk with this my lord? for as for me, straightway there remained no strength in me, neither was there breath left in me.

units.leftText: Again the one with the likeness of a man touched me and strengthened me.
units.rightText: Then there touched me again one like the appearance of a man, and he strengthened me.

units.leftText: “Do not be afraid, you who are highly precious,” he said. “Peace be with you! Be strong now; be very strong!” As he spoke with me, I was strengthened and said, “Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me.”
units.rightText: And he said, O man greatly beloved, fear not: peace be unto thee, be strong, yea, be strong. And when he spake unto me, I was strengthened, and said, Let my lord speak; for thou hast strengthened me.

units.leftText: “Do you know why I have come to you?” he said. “I must return at once to fight against the prince of Persia, and when I have gone forth, behold, the prince of Greece will come.
units.rightText: Then said he, Knowest thou wherefore I am come unto thee? and now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia: and when I go forth, lo, the prince of Greece shall come.
leftNotes: 10:20 Hebrew of Javan

units.leftText: But first I will tell you what is inscribed in the Book of Truth. Yet no one has the courage to support me against these, except Michael your prince.[’’]
units.rightText: But I will tell thee that which is inscribed in the writing of truth: and there is none that holdeth with me against these, but Michael your prince.

units.leftText: “And I, in the first year of Darius the Mede, stood up to strengthen and protect him.
units.rightText: And as for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to confirm and strengthen him.

units.leftText: Now then, I will tell you the truth: Three more kings will arise in Persia, and then a fourth, who will be far richer than all the others. By the power of his wealth, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
units.rightText: And now will I show thee the truth. Behold, there shall stand up yet three kings in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than they all: and when he is waxed strong through his riches, he shall stir up all against the realm of Greece.
leftNotes: 11:2 Hebrew of Javan

units.leftText: Then a mighty king will arise, who will rule with great authority and do as he pleases.
units.rightText: And a mighty king shall stand up, that shall rule with great dominion, and do according to his will.

units.leftText: But as soon as he is established, his kingdom will be broken up and parceled out toward the four winds of heaven. It will not go to his descendants, nor will it have the authority with which he ruled, because his kingdom will be uprooted and given to others.
units.rightText: And when he shall stand up, his kingdom shall be broken, and shall be divided toward the four winds of heaven, but not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion wherewith he ruled; for his kingdom shall be plucked up, even for others besides these.

units.leftText: The king of the South will grow strong, but one of his commanders will grow even stronger and will rule his own kingdom with great authority.
units.rightText: And the king of the south shall be strong, and one of his princes; and he shall be strong above him, and have dominion; his dominion shall be a great dominion.

units.leftText: After some years they will form an alliance, and the daughter of the king of the South will go to the king of the North to seal the agreement. But his daughter will not retain her position of power, nor will his strength endure. At that time she will be given up, along with her royal escort and her father and the one who supported her.
units.rightText: And at the end of years they shall join themselves together; and the daughter of the king of the south shall come to the king of the north to make an agreement: but she shall not retain the strength of her arm; neither shall he stand, nor his arm; but she shall be given up, and they that brought her, and he that begat her, and he that strengthened her in those times.
leftNotes: 11:6 Or offspring
11:6 Or child; see Vulgate and Syriac.

units.leftText: But one from her family line will rise up in his place, come against the army of the king of the North, and enter his fortress, fighting and prevailing.
units.rightText: But out of a shoot from her roots shall one stand up in his place, who shall come unto the army, and shall enter into the fortress of the king of the north, and shall deal against them, and shall prevail.
leftNotes: 11:7 Literally a branch from her roots

units.leftText: He will take even their gods captive to Egypt, with their metal images and their precious vessels of silver and gold. For some years he will stay away from the king of the North,
units.rightText: And also their gods, with their molten images, and with their goodly vessels of silver and of gold, shall he carry captive into Egypt; and he shall refrain some years from the king of the north.

units.leftText: who will invade the realm of the king of the South and then return to his own land.
units.rightText: And he shall come into the realm of the king of the south, but he shall return into his own land.

units.leftText: But his sons will stir up strife and assemble a great army, which will advance forcefully, sweeping through like a flood, and will again carry the battle as far as his fortress.
units.rightText: And his sons shall war, and shall assemble a multitude of great forces, which shall come on, and overflow, and pass through; and they shall return and war, even to his fortress.

units.leftText: In a rage, the king of the South will march out to fight the king of the North, who will raise a large army, but it will be delivered into the hand of his enemy.
units.rightText: And the king of the south shall be moved with anger, and shall come forth and fight with him, even with the king of the north; and he shall set forth a great multitude, and the multitude shall be given into his hand.

units.leftText: When the army is carried off, the king of the South will be proud in heart and will cast down tens of thousands, but he will not triumph.
units.rightText: And the multitude shall be lifted up, and his heart shall be exalted; and he shall cast down tens of thousands, but he shall not prevail.

units.leftText: For the king of the North will raise another army, larger than the first, and after some years he will advance with a great army and many supplies.
units.rightText: And the king of the north shall return, and shall set forth a multitude greater than the former; and he shall come on at the end of the times, even of years, with a great army and with much substance.
leftNotes: 11:13 Hebrew at the end of the times

units.leftText: In those times many will rise up against the king of the South. Violent ones among your own people will exalt themselves in fulfillment of the vision, but they will fail.
units.rightText: And in those times there shall many stand up against the king of the south: also the children of the violent among thy people shall lift themselves up to establish the vision; but they shall fall.

units.leftText: Then the king of the North will come, build up a siege ramp, and capture a fortified city. The forces of the South will not stand; even their best troops will not be able to resist.
units.rightText: So the king of the north shall come, and cast up a mound, and take a well-fortified city: and the forces of the south shall not stand, neither his chosen people, neither shall there be any strength to stand.

units.leftText: The invader will do as he pleases, and no one will stand against him. He will establish himself in the Beautiful Land, with destruction in his hand.
units.rightText: But he that cometh against him shall do according to his own will, and none shall stand before him; and he shall stand in the glorious land, and in his hand shall be destruction.

units.leftText: He will resolve to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and will reach an agreement with the king of the South. He will give him a daughter in marriage in order to overthrow the kingdom, but his plan will not succeed or help him.
units.rightText: And he shall set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and with him equitable conditions; and he shall perform them: and he shall give him the daughter of women, to corrupt her; but she shall not stand, neither be for him.
leftNotes: 11:17 Or but she will not stand with him or support him

units.leftText: Then he will turn his face to the coastlands and capture many of them. But a commander will put an end to his reproach and will turn it back upon him.
units.rightText: After this shall he turn his face unto the isles, and shall take many: but a prince shall cause the reproach offered by him to cease; yea, moreover, he shall cause his reproach to turn upon him.

units.leftText: After this, he will turn back toward the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and fall and be no more.
units.rightText: Then he shall turn his face toward the fortresses of his own land; but he shall stumble and fall, and shall not be found.

units.leftText: In his place one will arise who will send out a tax collector for the glory of the kingdom; but within a few days he will be destroyed, though not in anger or in battle.
units.rightText: Then shall stand up in his place one that shall cause an exactor to pass through the glory of the kingdom; but within few days he shall be destroyed, neither in anger, nor in battle.

units.leftText: In his place a despicable person will arise; royal honors will not be given to him, but he will come in a time of peace and seize the kingdom by intrigue.
units.rightText: And in his place shall stand up a contemptible person, to whom they had not given the honor of the kingdom: but he shall come in time of security, and shall obtain the kingdom by flatteries.

units.leftText: Then a flood of forces will be swept away before him and destroyed, along with a prince of the covenant.
units.rightText: And the overwhelming forces shall be overwhelmed from before him, and shall be broken; yea, also the prince of the covenant.

units.leftText: After an alliance is made with him, he will act deceitfully; for he will rise to power with only a few people.
units.rightText: And after the league made with him he shall work deceitfully; for he shall come up, and shall become strong, with a small people.

units.leftText: In a time of peace, he will invade the richest provinces and do what his fathers and forefathers never did. He will lavish plunder, loot, and wealth on his followers, and he will plot against the strongholds — but only for a time.
units.rightText: In time of security shall he come even upon the fattest places of the province; and he shall do that which his fathers have not done, nor his fathers’ fathers; he shall scatter among them prey, and spoil, and substance: yea, he shall devise his devices against the strongholds, even for a time.

units.leftText: And with a large army he will stir up his power and his courage against the king of the South, who will mobilize a very large and powerful army but will not withstand the plots devised against him.
units.rightText: And he shall stir up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south shall war in battle with an exceeding great and mighty army; but he shall not stand; for they shall devise devices against him.

units.leftText: Those who eat from his provisions will seek to destroy him; his army will be swept away, and many will fall slain.
units.rightText: Yea, they that eat of his dainties shall destroy him, and his army shall overflow; and many shall fall down slain.

units.leftText: And the two kings, with their hearts bent on evil, will speak lies at the same table, but to no avail, for still the end will come at the appointed time.
units.rightText: And as for both these kings, their hearts shall be to do mischief, and they shall speak lies at one table: but it shall not prosper; for yet the end shall be at the time appointed.

units.leftText: The king of the North will return to his land with great wealth, but his heart will be set against the holy covenant; so he will do damage and return to his own land.
units.rightText: Then shall he return into his land with great substance; and his heart shall be against the holy covenant; and he shall do his pleasure, and return to his own land.

units.leftText: At the appointed time he will invade the South again, but this time will not be like the first.
units.rightText: At the time appointed he shall return, and come into the south; but it shall not be in the latter time as it was in the former.

units.leftText: Ships of Kittim will come against him, and he will lose heart. Then he will turn back and rage against the holy covenant and do damage. So he will return and show favor to those who forsake the holy covenant.
units.rightText: For ships of Kittim shall come against him; therefore he shall be grieved, and shall return, and have indignation against the holy covenant, and shall do his pleasure: he shall even return, and have regard unto them that forsake the holy covenant.
leftNotes: 11:30 Or western coastlands or Mediterranean islands

units.leftText: His forces will rise up and desecrate the temple fortress. They will abolish the daily sacrifice and set up the abomination of desolation.
units.rightText: And forces shall stand on his part, and they shall profane the sanctuary, even the fortress, and shall take away the continual burnt-offering, and they shall set up the abomination that maketh desolate.

units.leftText: With flattery he will corrupt those who violate the covenant, but the people who know their God will firmly resist him.
units.rightText: And such as do wickedly against the covenant shall he pervert by flatteries; but the people that know their God shall be strong, and do exploits.

units.leftText: Those with insight will instruct many, though for a time they will fall by sword or flame, or be captured or plundered.
units.rightText: And they that are wise among the people shall instruct many; yet they shall fall by the sword and by flame, by captivity and by spoil, many days.

units.leftText: Now when they fall, they will be granted a little help, but many will join them insincerely.
units.rightText: Now when they shall fall, they shall be helped with a little help; but many shall join themselves unto them with flatteries.

units.leftText: Some of the wise will fall so that they may be refined, purified, and made spotless until the time of the end, for it will still come at the appointed time. The King Who Exalts Himself
units.rightText: And some of them that are wise shall fall, to refine them, and to purify, and to make them white, even to the time of the end; because it is yet for the time appointed.

units.leftText: Then the king will do as he pleases and will exalt and magnify himself above every god, and he will speak monstrous things against the God of gods. He will be successful until the time of wrath is completed, for what has been decreed must be accomplished.
units.rightText: And the king shall do according to his will; and he shall exalt himself, and magnify himself above every god, and shall speak marvellous things against the God of gods; and he shall prosper till the indignation be accomplished; for that which is determined shall be done.

units.leftText: He will show no regard for the gods of his fathers, nor for the one desired by women, nor for any other god, because he will magnify himself above them all.
units.rightText: Neither shall he regard the gods of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor regard any god; for he shall magnify himself above all.

units.leftText: And in their place, he will honor a god of fortresses— a god his fathers did not know— with gold, silver, precious stones, and riches.
units.rightText: But in his place shall he honor the god of fortresses; and a god whom his fathers knew not shall he honor with gold, and silver, and with precious stones and pleasant things.

units.leftText: He will attack the strongest fortresses with the help of a foreign god and will greatly honor those who acknowledge him, making them rulers over many and distributing the land for a price.
units.rightText: And he shall deal with the strongest fortresses by the help of a foreign god: whosoever acknowledgeth him he will increase with glory; and he shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for a price.
leftNotes: 11:39 Or for a reward

units.leftText: At the time of the end, the king of the South will engage him in battle, but the king of the North will storm out against him with chariots, horsemen, and many ships, invading many countries and sweeping through them like a flood.
units.rightText: And at the time of the end shall the king of the south contend with him; and the king of the north shall come against him like a whirlwind, with chariots, and with horsemen, and with many ships; and he shall enter into the countries, and shall overflow and pass through.
leftNotes: 11:40 Hebrew will thrust at him

units.leftText: He will also invade the Beautiful Land, and many countries will fall. But these will be delivered from his hand: Edom, Moab, and the leaders of the Ammonites.
units.rightText: He shall enter also into the glorious land, and many countries shall be overthrown; but these shall be delivered out of his hand: Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon.

units.leftText: He will extend his power over many countries, and not even the land of Egypt will escape.
units.rightText: He shall stretch forth his hand also upon the countries; and the land of Egypt shall not escape.

units.leftText: He will gain control of the treasures of gold and silver and over all the riches of Egypt, and the Libyans and Cushites will also submit to him.
units.rightText: But he shall have power over the treasures of gold and of silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt; and the Libyans and the Ethiopians shall be at his steps.
leftNotes: 11:43 That is, people from the upper Nile region

units.leftText: But news from the east and the north will alarm him, and he will go out with great fury to destroy many and devote them to destruction.
units.rightText: But tidings out of the east and out of the north shall trouble him; and he shall go forth with great fury to destroy and utterly to sweep away many.
leftNotes: 11:44 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.

units.leftText: He will pitch his royal tents between the sea and the beautiful holy mountain, but he will meet his end with no one to help him.[’’]
units.rightText: And he shall plant the tents of his palace between the sea and the glorious holy mountain; yet he shall come to his end, and none shall help him.

units.leftText: “At that time Michael, the great prince who stands watch over your people, will rise up. There will be a time of distress, the likes of which will not have occurred from the beginning of nations until that time. But at that time your people — everyone whose name is found written in the book — will be delivered.
units.rightText: And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who standeth for the children of thy people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.

units.leftText: And many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life, but others to shame and everlasting contempt.
units.rightText: And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
leftNotes: 12:2 See John 5:29|JHN 5:29* and Revelation 11:18.

units.leftText: Then the wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens, and those who lead many to righteousness will shine like the stars forever and ever.
units.rightText: And they that are wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.
leftNotes: 12:3 Or expanse or firmament; see also Genesis 1:6–8|GEN 1:6-8*.
12:3 See Matthew 13:43|MAT 13:43*.

units.leftText: But you, Daniel, shut up these words and seal the book until the time of the end. Many will roam to and fro, and knowledge will increase.”
units.rightText: But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased.

units.leftText: Then I, Daniel, looked and saw two others standing there, one on this bank of the river and one on the opposite bank.
units.rightText: Then I, Daniel, looked, and, behold, there stood other two, the one on the brink of the river on this side, and the other on the brink of the river on that side.

units.leftText: One of them said to the man dressed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, “How long until the fulfillment of these wonders?”
units.rightText: And one said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?

units.leftText: And the man dressed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven, and I heard him swear by Him who lives forever, saying, “It will be for a time, and times, and half a time. When the power of the holy people has finally been shattered, all these things will be completed.”
units.rightText: And I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware by him that liveth for ever that it shall be for a time, times, and a half; and when they have made an end of breaking in pieces the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.

units.leftText: I heard, but I did not understand. So I asked, “My lord, what will be the outcome of these things?”
units.rightText: And I heard, but I understood not: then said I, O my lord, what shall be the issue of these things?

units.leftText: “Go on your way, Daniel,” he replied, “for the words are closed up and sealed until the time of the end.
units.rightText: And he said, Go thy way, Daniel; for the words are shut up and sealed till the time of the end.

units.leftText: Many will be purified, made spotless, and refined, but the wicked will continue to act wickedly. None of the wicked will understand, but the wise will understand.
units.rightText: Many shall purify themselves, and make themselves white, and be refined; but the wicked shall do wickedly; and none of the wicked shall understand; but they that are wise shall understand.

units.leftText: And from the time the daily sacrifice is abolished and the abomination of desolation set up, there will be 1,290 days.
units.rightText: And from the time that the continual burnt-offering shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.

units.leftText: Blessed is he who waits and reaches the end of the 1,335 days.
units.rightText: Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days.

units.leftText: But as for you, go on your way until the end. You will rest, and then you will arise to your inheritance at the end of the days.”
units.rightText: But go thou thy way till the end be; for thou shalt rest, and shalt stand in thy lot, at the end of the days.
